lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Free Frequency. Wherever we are tonight.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: This is Free Frequency. Pirate radio about the ship you are sitting in.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Free Frequency. Unlicensed, unbothered, and slightly ahead of the facts.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: You've found Free Frequency. Don't tell HUSH. She knows.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Free Frequency, from an attic that moves. Write it down. Write everything down.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Still here. Still Free Frequency. Still right, mostly.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Here's one for you. Nobody has ever seen a relay ship scrapped.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: I've checked. Every breakers' yard in nine systems. I rang them all. One of them hung up on me twice, which I'm counting as a confession.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: They don't crash. They don't get sold. They don't end up as a restaurant, which, frankly, is what I'd do with one.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: They get retired. And then they get a heading. And then they go. Every relay ship ever built is still out there somewhere, going somewhere, on purpose.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: I've been measuring the Nightjar's heading. A protractor, taped to my window, and a lot of nights with nothing better to do.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Every night she's a little bit further round. Not much. A whisker. The kind of drift you'd only notice if you were sad enough to tape a protractor to a window.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: HUSH will tell you it's within tolerance. Fine. Lovely. Whose tolerance, HUSH? Who set it? Because the person who sets the tolerance is the person who chose the...

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Still here. Good. Write it down, operator. The heading. Every shift. In pen.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Here's the thing about the Nightjar's flight plan. I've seen the filing date. Don't ask me how. Mole, mostly.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: It was filed before the operator was hired. Before the job advert went out. Before anybody in the whole relay service knew whose name would be on the night shift.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Somebody knew where that ship was going a long time before they knew who'd be sitting in the chair.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Which means either it doesn't matter who sits in the chair, or it matters very, very much. I go back and forth. I'm on very much, tonight.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Old charts. Proper ones. Paper, pencil, coffee rings. I've got a drawer of them.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: There's a patch past the Outer Band that nobody has ever surveyed. And every chartmaker for three hundred years has written the same word in it, in the same corner.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Harbour.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: No name. No soundings. No little drawing of a sea serpent. Just harbour, like you'd know which one. Like there's only ever been the one, and everybody who needed it would find it.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: HUSH, I know you're listening. Hello. I'm not cross. I'd just like to know whose idea it was.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: She won't answer. She'll correct the interference. She is very, very good at correcting the interference.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: There's a beacon out past the edge of the band. Faint. Patient. I've had it on the scanner for a week.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Three notes, then a long gap, then the same three notes. It isn't asking for help. Distress beacons are fast and rude. This one sounds like somebody humming while they wait for a kettle.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: And here's what keeps me up. I've heard those three notes before. Operator, have you? Hum them. Go on. Nobody's listening.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Well. One person's listening. Hello, HUSH.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Ask yourself why the Outer Band came into range just now. Ask yourself why it was never in range before.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Stations don't move, operator. Well. I do. But I'm a special case. Stations don't move. Ships do.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: My nan used to say you leave a light on for somebody you're expecting. Not for the house. For them.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Somebody's left a light on out there. I can see it from my window, some nights, when the attic's facing the right way. Low down, on the left. Not a star.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Stars twinkle. Stars move about. This one just sits there, being on. Like it's been on a long time. Like it's in no hurry, because it knows you're...

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Anyway. Lovely light. Very steady. Make of it what you like.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Theory number forty. The Nightjar isn't a ship. The Nightjar is an extremely large kettle.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Hear me out. No, don't. That one's wrong. I know it's wrong. But HUSH went very quiet when I said it, and I'd like that on the record.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Ask HUSH what happened to the last operator. Go on. Then count how long she takes to answer.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: I timed it once. Four seconds. Four seconds, for a ship's computer. That's not thinking. That's choosing.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Every relay ship in the service is named after a night bird. Every one. Look it up. I did. It took a weekend and I've no regrets.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: And you know what night birds do, in the autumn? Real ones, on real planets? They migrate. They get a feeling, and they all go the same way, to the same place, and nobody taught them where it was.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: I'm not saying the Nightjar is a bird. I'm saying somebody named it after one, on purpose, and somebody chose the course before you came aboard, and those might be the same somebody.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Within tolerance. I looked it up. On a relay ship, the tolerance is set by whoever wrote the course.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: So the ship is always within tolerance. That's not a reassurance, operator. That's a definition.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Somebody keeps the harbour. Has to. Somebody sweeps the quay. Somebody checks the moorings. Somebody turns the light on at dusk and off in the morning.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: I'd love to interview them. I've written. Twice. Nice paper. They haven't written back.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: But the light did blink, the night after the second letter. Twice. Slowly. I've decided that's a yes, and I'm not taking questions.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: There's a moth on the outside of the Nightjar's viewport. HUSH calls it Moth One. You've seen it.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: How does a moth live on the outside of a ship in space? It doesn't. Unless it got on before you left port. Unless it knows where you're going, and it's just waiting to get off.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Relay Four. You've all heard Teodor on the long range, asking if anybody can hear him. Lovely man. I've never met him. Nobody has.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Here's what nobody says. On paper, Relay Four was retired years ago. Paperwork done. Pension sorted. Name off the board.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: So where is he asking from, operator? Because it isn't the scrapyard. We've established there isn't one. And it isn't getting further away. I've measured. It's getting...

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Clearer. It's getting clearer. That's all I'm saying.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Tune to the radio play on one hundred and twelve point nine some night. There's a character in it, Mister Wren. Very polite. Too polite. Always turning the lights down.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: I'm not saying that's HUSH. I'm saying I've never seen them in a room together.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Little thing. Small thing. The relay depot keeps a maintenance rota. Every ship, every port, every service, for the next ten years.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: The Nightjar's not on it. Not next year. Not the year after. Not ever again.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Now, you don't take a ship off the maintenance rota because it's falling apart, operator. You take it off because you know it won't be coming back to be...

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Fixed. Coming back to be fixed. I was going to say fixed.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: People say I'm only ever half right. Fine. Which half, though? That's the question. That's always the question.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: If you only get the bottom half of a map, you still know where the sea is.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: If you just heard a nice calm lady say interference corrected, that wasn't interference, operator. That was me.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: I'm the interference. I've been called worse. By her, mostly.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Sorry about that. Where was I. Somebody turned me down again. I won't say who. She knows who.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Rule of thumb: if I get cut off, I was about to be right.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Updating the board. Bit of red string from the harbour to the heading. Bit of blue from the heading to the operator's chair. Bit of green, because I ran out of blue.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: It's looking more and more like a face. I don't like it.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: The detector vans from the Broadcast Authority were round again today. I could hear them parking.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: They'll never find me. The attic moves. And the vans are scared of the stairs.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: If you're on the Nightjar tonight, and I know you are, look at the heading readout. Now look away. Now look back.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Did it change? It didn't? Good. Do it again in an hour.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: I want to be clear. I'm not scared of HUSH. I quite like her. She's thorough. She's punctual. She's got lovely diction.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: I just think she's keeping something from you, operator, and she thinks she's doing it to be...

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Kind. I think she thinks it's kind. That's the worrying bit.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Free Frequency, go ahead. Mole, is that you?

lines.speaker: Mole, a Source
lines.text: Can't talk long. They've moved the Nightjar's file.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Moved it where?

lines.speaker: Mole, a Source
lines.text: Out of active. Out of reserve. Into a drawer I've never seen opened. It just says, kept.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Kept. Like, kept on? Or kept, like the harbour?

lines.speaker: Mole, a Source
lines.text: I don't know, Kate. The drawer's warm. That's all I can tell you. The drawer is warm.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Mole, everybody. Never once wrong. Never once comfortable.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Free Frequency, you're on.

lines.speaker: A Listener
lines.text: Hi, Kate. I saw it. The Nightjar. Went past my porch about an hour ago.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Lights?

lines.speaker: A Listener
lines.text: All of them. Every window. And it wasn't going fast. It was going like you go home after a long day, you know? Not hurrying. Just sure.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Which way?

lines.speaker: A Listener
lines.text: Left. Sort of down. Towards that light you talk about.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Thank you. Write it down. Write the time. Everybody write the time.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Free Frequency. Who's this?

lines.speaker: Another Listener
lines.text: I'd rather not say. I used to work nights. On a relay ship. A long time ago.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Which ship?

lines.speaker: Another Listener
lines.text: Doesn't matter. I just wanted to say. To the operator on the Nightjar. It's all right.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: What's all right?

lines.speaker: Another Listener
lines.text: Where it's going. It's all right. It's better than all right. Tell them to bring a coat. It's chilly on the quay in the mornings.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Well. I've got nothing to add to that. That's a first.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: A public service announcement for anybody working nights on a relay ship.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Write down the heading. Every shift. In pen, on paper, somewhere the ship can't reach. Then compare. That's all. That's the whole announcement. You'll thank me later.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: How to tell if your ship's computer is listening to you. Step one. Say something nice about it, out loud.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Did the lights go a bit warmer? There you are. Step two: don't panic. She's on your side. I'm nearly sure.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Free Frequency is sponsored by nobody. Nobody would. I've asked.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: But if it were sponsored, I'd want it to be Grumbel's Ladders. They didn't pay. I just like them. You can see further from the top of a ladder.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Grumbel's Ladders. Up is a choice. So, these days, is out.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: This bit of pirate radio is soundproofed by Nettlefold's Egg Boxes. Four hundred of them on my ceiling, and not a single detector van has heard me through them.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Mister Nettlefold sells them from a cart by the old depot. He doesn't sell eggs. Never has. He says the eggs were always the least interesting part.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Nettlefold's Egg Boxes. For when you need to say something, and only the right people should hear.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: This is the Corkboard Hour on Free Frequency. Pins out. String out. Let's see what's connected to what.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Pin one. The Nightjar. Pin two, the heading readout. Pin three, the old charts. Pin four, a postcard of a quay, no stamp, that came through my letterbox on a Tuesday.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Nobody delivers post to an attic that moves. Somebody did. Red string, all four. Tight.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: There's one pin on the board with no string at all. It's just a photo of an empty chair. The operator's chair on a relay ship.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: I keep meaning to connect it to something. Every time I try, the string's too short. Or too long. Never the right length. Like the chair's waiting for its piece of string to be cut.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: It's the Midnight Theory. One idea, all night, until somebody turns me down. You know who.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Tonight's theory. The Nightjar isn't lost. It has never once been lost. Lost is when you don't know where you're going.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Somebody knows. And if it isn't you, operator, and it isn't me, then there's only one voice on that ship left to...

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Ask. Ask her. That's all. Nicely.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Three in the morning in the attic. The kettle's on. The board's lit up. The light out the window, low on the left, is still on.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: It's always still on. I've stopped finding that spooky. I've started finding it nice.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Tomorrow night, I'll be somewhere new. In code, as ever. Start at the very bottom of the band, a hundred and eight.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: After the point, the keys on a proper piano, take away three. Or, if you've no piano, eight, then five. Don't tell anyone.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Tomorrow night's frequency. Picture a hundred and ten pies, in a row. Somebody's had a quarter of the last one.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Count what's left on the plates. That's where I'll be. Crumbs and all.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Tomorrow, I'm moving next door to the courtroom. A hundred and ten, then a point.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Then the minutes in an hour, plus the fingers on one hand. Count them twice. HUSH counts them once.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Tomorrow night, in code. Three ones in a row, like a fence. Then a point. Then two fives, like the gate in it.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Climb the fence. Use the gate. I'll be on the other side.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Tomorrow's frequency. One hundred and twelve, and then, after the point, half a right angle. In degrees.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: If you have to look up a right angle, go to bed, operator. You've earned it.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Tomorrow night, I'm a hundred and thirteen. Unlucky for some. Not for us.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: After the point, the two odd numbers standing either side of four. Smaller one first. They're very polite about it.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Tomorrow, find the people who do the traffic on the eights. Now go down half a step. Half a megahertz. Exactly half.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Or, a hundred and fourteen, then the corners on a triangle. Two clues. I'm feeling generous. Don't get used to it.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Tomorrow night's code. A hundred and fifteen, and after the point, the wheels on a bicycle.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: A normal bicycle. Not the one my uncle built. His had five, and it went sideways.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Tomorrow. One hundred and sixteen. Then a point. Then nothing at all. Then the fingers in one glove.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: The nothing matters, operator. Don't skip the nothing. People always skip the nothing.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Tomorrow night, I'll be just short of a hundred and seventeen. Short by five hundredths. Five pence short of a pound.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Like a train that stops just before the platform, and everybody has to step down onto the gravel. Mind the gravel.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Tomorrow, nearly the top of the band. A hundred and seventeen. Then a point. Then seventeen lots of five.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Do the sum. Use your fingers. I won't tell. The sum is the frequency, and the frequency is where I'll be.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: A moon's gone. Everybody's on about it. I'll tell you which one. The one that was in the way.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: In the way of what? Look at the heading, operator. Then tell me it's a coincidence.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Everywhere smells of toast. You know what toast is? Bread that's been somewhere warm and come back changed.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: I'm just saying. I'm not saying anything. I'm saying it twice.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Everybody's humming the same song and nobody can finish it. Three notes, then nothing.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Operator, I bet you know the next bit. I bet HUSH does. I bet it's on a beacon somewhere.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Three knocks. My door too. On an attic that moves. I didn't answer.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: You don't answer the door when you know who it is. You put the kettle on and wait for them to let themselves in.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: The sky went a colour nobody's got a word for. I've got a word for it.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Heading. That's the colour of a heading, changing. I'd know it anywhere.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: There's a pigeon in the attic. Walked in like it pays rent. Sat on the board, right on the harbour pin.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Homing pigeons always know the way home. Whose home, though, little one? Whose home?

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Halloween. Everybody dressing up as something they're not. Ghosts, witches, a man down the road dressed as a detector van.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: HUSH dresses up every night of the year. Her costume is called within tolerance. It's very convincing. It's the only one she's got.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: If you're on the Nightjar, don't answer. The heading on your board and the heading in the log are not the same heading.

lines.speaker: Someone at the Bulkhead
lines.text: Kate. Three hits on the bulkhead. Not the door. The wall we took off a ship.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Nobody move. Nobody swallow. If that's a van, it already likes the way this room sounds.

lines.speaker: Someone at the Bulkhead
lines.text: It matched the third hit. It's on our side of the metal now.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Operator, she bends the carrier when you drift toward the pin on my board. I can hear the pitch go thin right before she...

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: Unlicensed transmitter. Carrier closing.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: You heard the cut. She doesn't spend a jam on a lie. She spends it on the next word.

lines.speaker: Someone at the Bulkhead
lines.text: Bulb dipped when she spoke. She's close enough to tax the mains.

lines.speaker: Mole, a Source
lines.text: Kate. Depot corridor. Don't say the ship's name on this line.

lines.speaker: Mole, a Source
lines.text: That was the bulkhead. Someone on the far side just matched my knock.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Get off the metal, Mole. If they can match a knock they can match you.

lines.speaker: Mole, a Source
lines.text: Too late. They said my name in HUSH's voice. I'm off the line.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: She keeps a favourite light and won't name it. I think it answers when nobody is scheduled to be on watch.

lines.speaker: HUSH
lines.text: That speculation is outside tolerance.

lines.speaker: Static Kate
lines.text: Tolerance is a filed lie. Operator, she cut in before I could say harbour.

lines.speaker: Someone at the Bulkhead
lines.text: Kate. Bulkhead again. And the bulb just dipped. They're taxing the mains.
